projects.name: FrameSeek
projects.title: Find the moment. Not just the video.
projects.description: A search engine that brings together what’s said, written, and seen in a video. Ask a question, refine it in conversation, and jump straight to the relevant moment.
projects.detail: Top-1 success measured once on 27 held-out test queries, using 79 AI-written labels audited by a random 20-label author spot check. The learned scorer beats fixed rank fusion but not transcript-only semantic search at top-1 (56%), and ties it at top-5 (67%). Runs locally with Docker Compose; no cloud deployment yet.
bullets: Built a video search engine that indexes speech (Whisper), on screen text (Tesseract OCR) and frames (OpenCLIP) into timestamped clips across five retrieval channels, with LangGraph conversational search over a custom LangChain retriever.

Engineered resumable ingestion on PostgreSQL with job leases, attempt generations, checksummed stage manifests and atomically published index versions, verified by worker crash, duplicate submission and failed reindex tests.
Developed a Go API with streaming uploads, SSRF safe URL import, idempotent jobs and signed media URLs in front of a Python FastAPI retrieval service on pgvector and PostgreSQL full text search.

Evaluated six retrieval arms on held out videos: a scikit-learn scorer over 25 cross modal features raised top 1 success from 26% to 48% over fixed rank fusion, while transcript only search reached 56% (79 AI written labels).

projects.name: StreamForge
projects.title: From live events to ready-to-use features.
projects.description: A distributed streaming pipeline that computes and serves fresh feature vectors for ML inference, with replicated state and low-latency retrieval.
projects.detail: All numbers from one shared 2 vCPU host. 250,000 synthetic events/sec held for 10 minutes with flat consumer lag; linearizable reads at 13 ms p99 under 1,000 req/s open loop load. Linearizability checked with Porcupine under leader kills, pauses and network partitions.
bullets: Built a real time feature store in Go and Kafka that computes per zone ML features from NYC taxi trips and serves them over gRPC; sustained 250,000 synthetic events/sec for 10 minutes with flat consumer lag on a 2 vCPU host.

Replicated the online store with a 5 node Raft group (PreVote, ReadIndex, snapshots, fsynced WAL) built without a consensus library; verified linearizability with Porcupine under leader kills, pauses and network partitions, with 381 ms median failover.

Achieved effectively once processing by committing Kafka offsets and window state atomically with feature updates in each Raft entry, yielding 0 mismatches against a batch oracle across 1M trips under repeated worker crashes.
Served linearizable reads at 13 ms p99 under 1,000 req/s open loop load, and added request coalescing that cut Redis cached p99 at 2,000 req/s from 33 ms to 22 ms.
